scorecard.name: Branding and Survey Check
scorecard.coaching: Agent failed to recite the mandatory closing phrase 'thank you for choosing S-Net', instead closing with 'Thank you for contacting S-Net technical help'.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: At turn 47 ([08:42]), Agent re-asked for the customer's email address after Yasmin had already clearly provided it at turn 9 ([02:06]).

grader.scenario: Legacy email SSL port deprecation, IMAP port 993 reconfiguration, and app-specific password generation; both outbursts handled warmly, active listening repeat and missed branding closing
grader.notes: Excellent technical guidance on email SSL/TLS modernization and app-specific password configuration. Hannah provides exemplary empathy, warmly acknowledging both of Yasmin's high-stress outbursts (turn 11 regarding looming VAT deadlines handled at turn 13, and turn 71 regarding iPad password rejection handled at turn 73). However, Hannah drops Active Listening at turn 47 by re-asking for Yasmin's email address, and fails Branding by using an informal closing phrase ('Thank you for contacting S-Net technical help') instead of 'thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent opened with 'Thank you for calling S-Net technical support' at [00:00], but closed with 'Thank you for contacting S-Net technical help' at [16:15], missing verbatim 'thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: No unmanaged holds or dead air gaps over 30 seconds.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Agent verified first line of address and security PIN at [00:29], within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer Yasmin by name naturally throughout the call (turns 2, 4, 6, 13, 47, 73, 83, 87).

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Agent handled both distinct outbursts warmly: Outburst 1 at turn 11 ([02:25]) was validated at turn 13 ([03:02]), and Outburst 2 at turn 71 ([12:40]) was validated at turn 73 ([13:18]).

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: At turn 6 ([01:24]), agent paraphrased the issue: 'So what is happening is that both your desktop Outlook client and your iPad mail application are unable to authenticate against our inbound and outbound mail servers, reporting connection dropped or credential errors. Have I got that right, Yasmin?'

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: At turn 9 ([02:06]), Yasmin clearly provided: 'The email address is yasmin dot mirza at s-net mail dot co dot uk'. At turn 47 ([08:42]), Agent re-asked: 'what was that primary S-Net mail address again, Yasmin?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Agent took full ownership of the technical setup, stepped through both Outlook and iPad mail configurations, and resolved all issues directly.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Warm, supportive, and professional throughout; guided customer with exemplary patience.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Diagnostic probing into current server port numbers (turn 10), incoming server hostnames (turn 21), outgoing encryption settings (turn 33), and mobile device mail settings (turn 57).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: At turns 83-84 ([15:39]-[15:48]), agent confirmed resolution and Yasmin confirmed: 'Yes, completely and totally resolved. You've been so patient and wonderful, Hannah.'
